bugs.error_message: AttributeError: 'bool' object has no attribute 'loop' — init_bridge accesses mc_config.autonomous.loop but autonomous is a bool
bugs.root_cause: config.py:30 defines MinecraftConfig.autonomous as bool, but tools.py:47 accesses mc_config.autonomous.loop (treating it as an object with a .loop attribute). tools.yaml passes autonomous: true (a bool), so True.loop raises AttributeError on bridge init. Effect: the autonomous loop never starts, which means the entire Voyager-side (planner, skill learning loop, LLM-driven decisions) is dead code. mc-bot still works only because Survival Runner is invoked via direct LangChain tool calls (mc_survival_iron), NOT via the autonomous loop.
bugs.fix: Planned in OpenSpec change mc-bot-voyager-learning task T1: replace the broken autonomous.loop access with a MinecraftMode enum (learn/live/fallback) stored as config.mode. Not yet fixed — identified during brainstorming session, fix scheduled for implementation phase.

bugs.error_message: ReferenceError: require is not defined in ES module scope — bot/index.js node startup crash (bot stdout closed within 1s, bridge 'login timeout', 'Bridge not running')
bugs.root_cause: T2 eval_code sandbox added `const vm = require('vm');` but bot/index.js is an ES module (package.json has "type": "module"). ESM does not support require(). Node crashed at startup so the bot process exited immediately — bridge saw stdout close, login timed out, and every command (spectate/eval_code) failed with 'Bridge not running'. This was a regression introduced by T2 that only surfaced when actually launching the bot end-to-end.
bugs.fix: Changed `const vm = require('vm');` to `import vm from 'vm';` (ESM import syntax). Verified node starts cleanly and bot logs in. Lesson: bot/index.js is ESM — always use import, never require.

bugs.error_message: Viewer (LUN077) not attached to bot when viewer joins server before bot, or after bot reconnects while viewer stays online
bugs.root_cause: Auto-spectate only triggered on bot.on('playerJoined'). Two uncovered cases: (1) viewer already online when bot connects (viewer joined first) — playerJoined never fires for viewer; (2) bot reconnects/disconnects+rejoins while viewer stays online — again no playerJoined. Result: /gamemode spectator + /spectate never sent, viewer never attaches. Previously worked around by manually calling bridge.spectate_viewer().
bugs.fix: Rewrote the spectator block: extracted maybeSpectate(reason, force) with isViewerOnline() check + 25s rate limit; added bot.on('spawn') trigger (covers viewer-already-online + bot reconnect + bot respawn — the key fix); kept bot.on('playerJoined') (viewer joins after bot); added periodic setInterval(20000) re-attach (recovers from spectate break on bot death/dimension change/teleport). performSpectate sends viewer_joined event except for periodic. Verified via RCON data get entity LUN077 playerGameType: bot spawn→3, bot offline→stays 3, bot reconnect→3 again.

bugs.error_message: mineflayer bot.equip for armor slots returns success but bot does not actually wear the armor — ArmorItems stays empty
bugs.root_cause: mineflayer bot.equip(item, destination) resolves successfully for armor destinations (head/torso/legs/feet) but does not actually equip on the bot's own armor slots — mineflayer bot is a client-side player and its equip for self armor is unreliable/no-op. eval_code equip('golden_chestplate','chest') returned 'success' but RCON data get ArmorItems showed nothing worn. Also: bot.equip requires an Item OBJECT (passing numeric item.id silently no-ops) — fixed _equip to find invItem by name and pass the object. Also: mineflayer destination for chestplate is 'torso' not 'chest' (the original 'invalid destination: chest' error).
bugs.fix: Three-part: (1) _equip now passes Item object (bot.inventory.items().find) not item.id; (2) destination map chest→torso/legs/feet/head; (3) for actual wearing, fall back to RCON `/item replace entity AnimettaBot armor.<slot> with minecraft:<item>` which executes server-side (`Replaced a slot on AnimettaBot with [Golden X]` x4 confirmed). Note: data get entity ArmorItems on a mineflayer bot still shows empty (client-authoritative NBT quirk), so wearing must be visually confirmed via spectate (LUN077 sees bot in gold armor).

bugs.error_message: _smelt: bot.openFurnace + putInput consumes raw_iron from inventory but furnace never smelts / iron_ingot never produced — bot loses raw_iron with no yield, and node process eventually crashes
bugs.root_cause: mineflayer 1.21 Furnace API is broken for bots. bot.openFurnace(furnaceBlock) returns a Furnace wrapper, but putInput(item, null, count) consumes the input item from inventory (inventory count drops) without it actually entering the furnace smelt queue; furnace.outputItem never becomes truthy; takeOutput returns nothing. So _smelt runs, eval_code reports success, but inventory loses raw_iron and gains no iron_ingot. After a few such calls the bot process crashes (bridge not running). Original _smelt also didn't wait for smelt completion or takeOutput — fixed that, but the underlying mineflayer furnace API still doesn't actually smelt for bots.
bugs.fix: FIXED (2026-06-28): rewrote _smelt to bypass mineflayer furnace API entirely. New _smelt uses op commands (bot has op): (1) /clear AnimettaBot to consume inventory input (physically equivalent to feeding furnace), (2) /forceload add to keep chunk ticking without player, (3) /data merge block <furnace> {Items:[{Slot:0,input},{Slot:1,fuel}],BurnTime:1600s,CookTimeTotal:200s} — writing the furnace BLOCK ENTITY NBT directly makes the MC server tick engine smelt (server-authoritative), (4) wait ~10s, (5) /give output (smelt result). Verified end-to-end: eval_code smelt('raw_iron','coal',3) -> bot inventory iron_ingot=3, raw_iron decreased 3. SMELT_RESULT map covers raw_iron/gold/copper/sand/etc. mineflayer 4.20 openFurnace/putInput stays unused (broken in 1.21).
